sections.heading: 1. Physical and Chemical Changes
points: **Physical change** — only **physical properties** (shape, size, state) change; **no new substance** is formed; usually **reversible**.
Examples: melting ice, dissolving sugar, tearing paper, folding, boiling water.
**Chemical change (chemical reaction)** — a **new substance** with new properties is formed; usually **irreversible**; often accompanied by heat/light/gas/colour change.
Examples: burning paper, cooking food, rusting of iron, souring of milk, digestion.

sections.heading: 2. Rusting of Iron
points: **Rusting** = iron reacting with **oxygen and moisture (water)** in air to form **rust (iron oxide)** — a **chemical change**.
**Both oxygen and water (moisture) are needed** for rusting.
Rusting is faster in **humid/coastal** areas.

sections.heading: 3. Preventing Rusting
points: **Painting, greasing/oiling** — form a barrier from air/water.
**Galvanisation** — coating iron with a layer of **zinc**.
**Chrome plating / making stainless steel** (alloying iron with chromium and nickel).

sections.heading: 4. Crystallisation
points: **Crystallisation** = obtaining **large pure crystals** of a substance from its solution (e.g. **salt from seawater**, **copper sulphate** crystals).
It is an example of a **physical change** used to purify substances.
Other reactions in the chapter: burning of magnesium ribbon → white **magnesium oxide** (a base); adding water → **magnesium hydroxide** (chemical changes).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Physical change = no new substance, reversible (melting, dissolving); chemical change = new substance, usually irreversible (burning, rusting).
Rusting = iron + oxygen + water → rust (iron oxide); needs BOTH oxygen & moisture.
Prevent rust: paint, grease, galvanise (zinc coat), stainless steel.
Crystallisation = large pure crystals from solution (physical change).
Cooking, souring of milk, digestion = chemical changes.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Rusting needs BOTH oxygen AND water (moisture)** — either alone will not rust iron.
**Galvanisation** = coating with **zinc**.
**Crystallisation** is a **physical** change (used for purification).
A change that forms a **new substance** (burning, rusting, cooking) is **chemical**.
